record.summary: AI chapter of a 2022 digital-governance law (Articles 3-14). Public-sector bodies may use AI systems to take or support decisions affecting a person's rights only where a specific law expressly allows it with safeguards; the defence and citizen-protection ministries and the intelligence service are excluded. Before use a body must carry out an algorithmic impact assessment, publish information about the system and keep a register of its systems, and contractors must disclose how systems work. Private employers must inform workers and candidates before using AI that affects decisions about them, and medium and large firms must register AI used for consumer profiling or staff evaluation.
record.notes: Signed on 26 July 2022 and published on 27 July 2022; the AI chapter applied from 1 January 2023 (Article 116(2)). The National Transparency Authority handles complaints about breaches of the public-sector transparency duties. The rest of the law covers cybersecurity, Internet of Things devices, unmanned aircraft for postal services, distributed ledger technology, 3D printing and other digital-governance matters. Chapter B of Part A was repealed by Article 26 of Law 5321/2026 from 20 July 2026, which re-established the public-sector AI register and the AI Observatory and set up the AI Act supervisory structure.

verification.note: Recheck of 17 Oct 2026: re-read the Government Gazette PDF of Law 4961/2022 (ΦΕΚ Α΄ 146/27.07.2022, 44 pages) stored on 12 Oct 2026 from the National Printing House file store and unchanged on 17 Oct, and stored for this record on 17 Oct 2026 the Government Gazette of Law 5321/2026 (ΦΕΚ Α΄ 114/20.07.2026, the same file as GR-01's). The first confirms the title, number, dates, signatures, the full text of Articles 3-14 and Article 116 on entry into force; the second confirms the repeal of the AI chapter by Article 26 and the new register and observatory (Articles 21-22). No English translation of the law was found.

judgment.status_reasoning: Article 26 of Law 5321/2026 (ΦΕΚ Α΄ 114/20.07.2026, stored for this record) repeals Chapter B of Part A of Law 4961/2022 from that law's entry into force on 20 July 2026, and Articles 21-22 re-establish its register and observatory under the AI Act implementation framework. The record covers the AI chapter, which has been replaced, so 'Superseded' stands.
judgment.scope_reasoning: AI-specific statutory provisions on public-sector and workplace use of AI; in scope with no note. Kept after repeal as a superseded instrument (AGENTS.md section 4, rule 7).
judgment.date_reasoning: date_published is the gazette date (27 July 2022), date_in_force the AI chapter's commencement under Article 116(2) (1 January 2023), date_last_updated the repeal by Law 5321/2026 (20 July 2026).
